subject: Dashboard signal: May KPI review & QBR readiness
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sam.holt@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dashboard signal: May KPI review & QBR readiness

Team — attaching the May dashboard export and a short note for QBR prep. TL;DR: two signals to flag before the review:

1) Latency: EU tail latency spike on 2027-05-07 between 03:00–04:30 UTC; p95 jumped ~220ms above baseline for medium-length chat sessions. Not reflected in error budget, but worth a root-cause check (kernel selection + hot shard?).

2) Cost: token spend is up ~14% MoM for Hosted API. Early signal points to an increase in small-batch calls (high per-request overhead) from a new partner integration (Acme Cloud).

Uptime: overall service SLOs held at 99.96% for the period; one short degraded window (2027-05-03 18:20 UTC) that was a regional NIC flail — Ops already applied a soft-failover.

Asks ahead of Wednesday's QBR prep: please confirm owners and quick remediation steps by EOD Tuesday so I can consolidate for the leadership deck. Suggested assignment:
- Root-cause for EU latency spike: markus
- Cost pattern and partner call-down with Acme: lauren (will loop Acme)

Attachments: 2027-05-kpi-dashboard.pdf (dashboard export), qbr-prep-notes.docx

Thanks —
Camila
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sam.holt@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dashboard signal: May KPI review & QBR readiness

Got it, Camila — thanks for the summary. I can own the Acme cost pattern. Quick questions:
- Do we have a breakdown by endpoint (generate vs embeddings) for the small-batch spike?
- Any specific client IDs that are driving the increase?

I'll reach out to Sam for a quick sync and ask for request traces for the window you flagged. If we confirm it's an integration pattern (lots of low-token calls), we should propose batching suggestions and a short-term quota throttle to limit immediate cost exposure.

I'll confirm by EOD Tuesday with a proposed cadence for a partner call.

—Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the heads-up — we saw the same small-batch pattern on our side after a recent SDK change. I'm looping ops@acmecloud.com; attached is a short runbook excerpt that shows the client-side batch window we enabled by default. We can toggle that back while we work through more efficient batching.

On latency: our traces show a few retries in the EU region in that window which amplified downstream tail latency. We'll pull the full trace bundle and share by EOD.
